newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Forecast late rain key to Argentine wheat-official.
newsitem.headline: Forecast late rain key to Argentine wheat-official.

text.p: Large parts of Argentina's wheat belt will need long-term forecasts of a wet spring to come true if they are to recover from drought, a government climate official said Wednesday.

"Those zones which are affected (by drought) today are going to find that the success or failure of their crop...will depend on the rain next spring," Cesar Rebella, head of the Agriculture Secretariat's climate section, told a news conference.
He said international forecasters were predicting a possible El Nino effect during Argentina's winter, which should mean average rainfall and no severe cold.
But, in drought-hit areas such as northern Buenos Aires province and central Santa Fe province, he said normal winter rainfall will not replenish soil moisture enough for wheat to prosper.
Fortunately, longer term forecasts suggest a wet spring, Rebella said. "We can expect a good chance of opportune and abundant rain at the start of the warmer weather."
Argentine farmers have still to start sowing 1997/98 wheat, after a bumper 1996/97 season, with output of 15.8 million tonnes.
